slot.brief: Compute ionisation potential/radius/energy for hydrogen-like ion (He+, Li2+) using Bohr formula scaling with Z and n.

stem: In a hydrogen-like ion, the electron transition from \(n = 2\) to \(n = 1\) emits a photon of wavelength \(30.4\ \text{nm}\) as shown in the figure. Given \(hc = 1240\ \text{eV\cdot nm}\), the ionisation energy of the ion in the ground state is:

verdicts.working: Photon energy: 1240/30.4 ≈ 40.8 eV. The n=2→1 transition releases 3/4 of the ground-state ionisation energy, so it is (4/3)(40.8) ≈ 54.4 eV.

working:
Photon energy \(\Delta E = hc/\lambda = 1240/30.4 = 40.8\ \text{eV}\). For hydrogen-like ion, \(\Delta E_{2\to1} = 13.6\,Z^2(1 - 1/4) = \frac{3}{4}\times 13.6\,Z^2\). Solving: \(Z^2 = 40.8 \times 4 / (13.6 \times 3) = 4\), so \(Z = 2\). Ground state ionisation energy \(= 13.6\,Z^2 = 54.4\ \text{eV}\).

Independent check: Photon energy: 1240/30.4 ≈ 40.8 eV. The n=2→1 transition releases 3/4 of the ground-state ionisation energy, so it is (4/3)(40.8) ≈ 54.4 eV.
solution:
The photon energy is $\Delta E=hc/\lambda=1240/30.4=40.8\,\text{eV}$. For a hydrogen-like ion, the $2\to1$ transition releases $\tfrac34$ of its ground-state ionisation energy:
$$E_{\text{ion}}=\frac{4}{3}\Delta E=\frac{4}{3}(40.8)=54.4\,\text{eV}.$$
